title: Apollo Hospitals to add 5,800 beds in next 5 years as revenue soars to ₹7043 crore in Q1FY27
summary: The expansion includes adding 148 beds to its existing facilities in Indore and Guwahati, along with four new hospitals in Indore, Dwarka, Delhi Proton Centre and Ranchi, together totalling 1,200 beds.

New Delhi: Apollo Hospitals said it plans to add over 5,800 total beds to its portfolio over the next five years as it reported an 21 per cent increase in year on year (YoY) consolidated revenue to Rs 7,043 crore in the first quarter ended June this year.The expansion includes adding 148 beds to its existing facilities in Indore and Guwahati, along with four new hospitals in Indore, Dwarka, Delhi Proton Centre and Ranchi, together totalling 1,200 beds.

This comes as the healthcare giant’s consolidated ebitda grew 28 per cent YoY to Rs 1,092 crore, while consolidated profit after tax stood at Rs 581 crore.

Advt

Apollo’s healthcare services arm reported a growth of 22 per cent in YoY revenue to Rs 3,567 crore.While ebitda grew 20 per cent YoY to Rs 862 crore, and PAT was up 25 per cent YoY to Rs 480 crore.

The corporate hospital chain said that as of June 30, 2026, Apollo Hospitals had 8,352 operating beds across the network, excluding its Apollo Health and Lifestyle Limited (AHLL) segment and managed beds, overall occupancy was at 70 per cent as compared to 65 per cent in Q1 FY26. The healthcare giant’s AHLL segment reported a growth of 15 per cent YoY in revenue to Rs 499 crore. Ebitda stood at Rs 59 crore as compared to Rs 40 crore in Q1FY26.

Under this vertical, diagnostics revenue stood at Rs 200 crore and spectra revenue at Rs 80 crore.The segment reported a PAT loss of Rs 1 crore during the quarter as compared to PAT loss of Rs 8 crore last year.The brand’s Apollo HealthCo segment saw a 20 per cent YoY growth in revenue to Rs 2,977 crore. While ebitda stood at Rs 171 crore, up from Rs 94 crore in Q1 FY26.

PAT was Rs 101 Crore as compared to Rs 57 crore during the same period last year.Apollo said the vertical continued to strengthen its omnichannel pharmacy and digital healthcare platform, with 151 net new stores added during the quarter, taking the network to 7,440 stores.

Advt

Dr. Prathap C. Reddy, Founder & Chairman, Apollo Hospitals Group, said, “The rising burden of non-communicable diseases and growing need for specialised care require us to move beyond episodic treatment towards a model that connects prevention, early diagnosis, advanced intervention and long-term care.

“Apollo’s integrated healthcare ecosystem is well placed to support this shift. Above all, these results reflect the enduring trust that patients and their families place in us. That trust remains our greatest responsibility.“During the quarter, we continued to expand access to advanced care with the commissioning of our hospitals in Sarjapur, Bangalore in Q1 FY27. Apollo now has plans to add over 5,800 total beds over the next 5 years.”
